## 

Sediment deposition was approximated as a rate from the original grams measurement, divided by the number of days deployed, multiplied by 1000 to go from a cm to a meter rate at each replicate tile per distance along the transect to result in a daily rate of sediment deposition per tile. Surface area was calculated from the surface area of the filter placed ( ) subtracted by the surface area of the rubber band used ( ). Each replicate tile was averaged together as a group of three into one distance measurement. Elevation at each replicate tile was also averaged into one distance metric.

Modeling for all testing factors driving sediment deposition were within a comparable general linear mixed models using a Gamma family distribution due to the positive, skewed distribution of the data. Transect was considered a replicate of Site level variance, and when appropriate was nested with Site within models. A factor of "Loc_ID" were used in addition to each entry that encompassed detail of the samples Replicate, Distance from Edge, Transect, and Site so as to avoid Pseudoreplication within the models.

Initially to test marsh edge type across rates of sediment deposition, we compared the distribution of data and the statistical traits. Additionally to test the effect of marsh edge type on rates of sediment deposition, we ran general linear mixed models at the Site level, with Transect as a nested effect within the Site level. We also incorporated added fixed and random effects of California Seasonality as per Lacy et al 2019's designation (will make a table), Distance from marsh edge, and z\* (Elevation relative to tidal inundation).

With the combined dataset between 2022-2023 and 2025-2026 collection between Corte Madera and San Pablo, the marsh edge general linear mixed model was repeated. In addition, Year was added as a fixed effect to test if the sediment deposition changed over time across each marsh.

Within the 2025-2026 collection, Distance and z\* were used in a generalized linear model with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression to determine if intra-marsh features had a greater significance as a factor for sediment deposition than marsh edge type.
